title: Blomqvist wins Oschersleben Race 2 as BMW sweep the top four
dek: Rookie Tom Blomqvist passed pole-sitter Augusto Farfus at the first corner and won his first DTM race by 7.712 seconds, before Lucas Auer's late crash brought out the red flag.

chapters.title: BMW's Saturday sets up a second sweep attempt
text: Saturday had belonged to BMW. Timo Glock won Race 1 from pole, seven BMWs finished in the first eight places, and Pascal Wehrlein's fifth place, driven with a failing power steering, put him at the head of the championship on 130 points, four clear of Mattias Ekström. Ekström had started 23rd and finished 14th.

Race 1 had consequences for Sunday: Mike Rockenfeller was given a three-place grid penalty for the first-corner collision and Robert Wickens a penalty of thirteen places. The second race ran for 60 minutes plus a lap and included a mandatory pit stop, so stop timing mattered as much as the start on a track where passing is hard.

chapters.title: Farfus takes pole by 0.019 seconds
text: Augusto Farfus put his BMW Team RBM car on pole with a 1m20.632s lap, 0.019 seconds faster than team-mate Tom Blomqvist, who lined up alongside him on the front row. The day before Farfus had qualified second and lost places at the first corner, and he said he wanted to turn this pole into the win.

Wehrlein was third on 1m20.659s, 0.027 seconds off the top, and said a small error on his last lap had cost him pole. António Félix da Costa was fourth, Paul di Resta fifth in the second Mercedes, Marco Wittmann sixth and Glock seventh. Christian Vietoris was eighth, Miguel Molina the best Audi in ninth and Bruno Spengler tenth. As on Saturday, the BMWs benefited from lighter weights: Farfus's car was around 30 kg lighter than Ekström's Audi.

Ekström had a difficult session and could do no better than 18th, 0.521 seconds off the pole time. Mortara was 16th fastest and started 15th. Rockenfeller was 13th fastest but his penalty put him 16th on the grid, behind Green, who started 13th. Wickens was last on 1m22.893s, more than two seconds slower than Farfus.

chapters.title: Blomqvist beats Farfus into turn one
text: Blomqvist made the better start and took the lead at the first corner. Farfus held second, with Félix da Costa third and Wittmann fourth after gaining two places off the line, while Wehrlein, who had started third, dropped to fifth in the opening moments. A tangle in the same area ended the races of Molina and Nico Müller, whose Audis both stopped before completing a lap, and the safety car came out.

Order at the restart was Blomqvist, Farfus, Félix da Costa and Wittmann, with Wehrlein going slightly wide at the first corner but keeping fifth. Blomqvist then started to pull clear of Farfus and built a lead through the first half of the race.

chapters.title: Wittmann gets past at the stops, Wehrlein's light stays dark
text: The mandatory stops reshuffled the middle of the field. Wittmann got ahead of Félix da Costa around the stops and took third place, a move he later put down to his pit stop. Wehrlein, meanwhile, came out of the pit lane without the tyre-change light illuminated, and his crew had to tell him to switch it on from the cockpit; the stewards investigated the delay after the race.

Martin Tomczyk was given a drive-through penalty for an unsafe release as he left his box with Paul di Resta alongside, and dropped to 20th at the finish. Jamie Green worked his way up from 13th on the grid with a series of overtakes, and a fast stop helped. He spent much of the race holding off Maxime Martin's significantly lighter BMW. Edoardo Mortara's Audi was parked in the garage about halfway through the race and he was out after 21 laps. Once the stops were done, Blomqvist had nearly five seconds in hand over his pursuers.

chapters.title: Auer's crash ends the race early
text: Blomqvist won by 7.712 seconds from Farfus, with Wittmann third at 13.080 and Félix da Costa fourth at 18.820, giving BMW the top four for the second day running. Félix da Costa had to resist heavy pressure from Wehrlein for much of the second half and the Mercedes driver finished fifth, 19.486 seconds behind the winner, ahead of Paul di Resta in sixth. Glock was seventh, Green eighth, Martin ninth and Spengler tenth, who held off Ekström for the last point.

The finish was cut short. Lucas Auer left the track without any contact in the closing stages and hit the tyre barrier at high speed, and the race was red-flagged. Auer got out of his Mercedes on his own and was classified 17th. Blomqvist's time of 57m30.221s for 40 laps stood as the winning time, and he had set the fastest lap, a 1m22.388s on lap 17.

chapters.title: A rookie's first win and a bigger lead for Wehrlein
text: Tom Blomqvist, 21, had finished seventh the day before, and called his first DTM victory perhaps the biggest day of his career so far. He was the tenth different winner in 14 races this season. Farfus said Blomqvist had been flying and deserved it, and BMW Team RBM added a one-two a day after BMW Team MTEK had done the same, with BMW taking the top four places in both races of the weekend. Farfus left with 30 points from the two races, and Wittmann's third took him to 98 points. Blomqvist said it reminded him of his Formula 3 days: in clear air he could use the full potential of the car, whereas in the midfield he had to cope with DRS and traffic all year.

Wehrlein's fifth place, his second of the weekend, extended his championship lead to 14 points. He had 140 points to Ekström's 126, and Ekström went home from Oschersleben without scoring in either race. Mortara was third on 110, Green fourth on 107, Spengler fifth on 104 and Wittmann sixth on 98, so six drivers from all three makes were within 42 points of the lead with four races left. A €1,000 fine followed for the late tyre-change light, but Wehrlein said that in terms of the championship he could be satisfied, even if the pace had not been what he hoped.

Audi's weekend ended on a thin note, with Green eighth the only Audi to score. Mercedes had Wehrlein and di Resta in the points, and its DTM head Ulrich Fritz said the race had been lost at the start, when Vietoris and Paffett had both lost ground and damaged their cars in the first-corner contact. Mercedes said Auer was unhurt after his accident, though he went for further checks as a precaution.
The DTM returns in two weeks at the Nürburgring on 26–27 September for the penultimate weekend, and the season finishes at Hockenheim on 17–18 October.

facts.v: Tom Blomqvist passed pole-sitter Farfus at the first corner and won his first DTM race in his rookie season by 7.712 seconds.

facts.v: At 21 years of age Blomqvist became the youngest BMW driver to win a DTM race, with only Pascal Wehrlein younger among all winners, and BMW's 68th DTM victory.
